cycle.label: Fall 2025 entering class (Class of 2029)
cycle.doc: Caltech Common Data Set 2025-26 (August 2026), C1: 7,772 men + 3,513 women applied; 224 + 204 admitted; 136 + 112 enrolled (unknown-sex rows blank; totals are the sums of the published lines)

scores.doc: CDS 2025-26, C9 (190 SAT submitters, 55 ACT submitters)

testPolicy.text: Caltech requires either SAT or ACT scores; applicants who have taken AP or IB exams are asked to submit those scores too. Testing must be completed before November 30 (REA) or December 31 (RD).

cost.totalIncludes: Undergraduate living in Caltech-owned housing, nine months: direct costs 93,225 (tuition 68,574 + fees 2,655 + housing 12,711 + food 9,285) + indirect costs 5,397 (books, course materials, supplies and equipment 1,428 + personal 3,969); the 98,622 total is the sum of the two published subtotals. Not included: Caltech Student Health Insurance Plan 5,388 (if no comparable coverage), one-time 600 orientation fee for entering students (CDS G1 first-year fees 3,255 = 2,655 + 600), optional computer allowance, and a travel allowance for US/Canada/Mexico residents.

aidPromise.text: Caltech meets 100% of demonstrated need (grants, scholarships, work-study and loans) and gives no merit scholarships. Most students from families making less than $200,000 (typical assets) can expect aid covering tuition; under $100,000, a no-loan package covering tuition, fees, housing and food. Need-blind for domestic students (including undocumented and DACA students graduating from a US high school); need-aware for international students.

deadlines.early: November 1, 2026 (Restrictive Early Action, non-binding, decision mid-December)

facts.text: Caltech is tiny: only 248 first-year students enrolled in fall 2025, from 11,285 applicants and 428 admits (3.8%).
Admission is need-blind for US students but need-aware for international applicants, because international aid funds are limited.

Families under $100,000 can expect a no-loan package covering tuition, fees, housing and food; under $200,000, aid typically covers tuition. Above that, Caltech packages can include loans, and there are no merit scholarships.
The 2026-27 cost of attendance is $98,622 on campus, and the Caltech Student Health Insurance Plan adds $5,388 for students without comparable coverage.
Restrictive Early Action is non-binding (admitted students have until May 1 and can compare aid offers), but most Caltech admits apply in Regular Decision.
The waiting list barely moves: 263 applicants were offered a place for fall 2025, 211 accepted and 1 was admitted.

notes: CDS link found on Princeton IR's peer CDS page (iro.caltech.edu). Parts of the PDF text use an encoded font (letters shifted), but all numeric values used here read cleanly. C1 unknown-sex rows and the residency table are blank/0, so totals are sums of men + women (applicants 11,285, admitted 428, enrolled 248). SAT composite percentiles not reported (sections only). The 98,622 COA total is computed from the two published subtotals (93,225 + 5,397); the page does not print a grand total line in the text I extracted. testPolicy.since null: the requirements page gives no start date; no announcement opened (web search quota exhausted). Average grant for incoming fall 2026 class 'just under $69,000' and 20% Pell-eligible are on the afford page. Accessed 2026-10-13.
